agent_note: Prose fiction, not verse. Reads as a linked collection rather than a single novel -- several unrelated casts (Sue Gliebe/Bob Roy, Anna, Kirk, Steve Wong, Bert) -- but the narration is consistently past tense across all of them, in both third person and first. 16 of 18 event quotes past (88.9%). The two present quotes (q01830, q01831) share a first-person essayistic voice and look like one distinct piece in the collection, not a competing narrating position. Two Russian-language quotes discarded as paratext -- a clear translated-edition leak onto the work page. Four quotes (q01820, q01823, q01824, q01843) are close calls on the quotation-mark majority test; all four resolve to event/past because the surrounding narration is past-tense either way, so the dialogue-test outcome does not change the label. No single quote flips this book: it would take three additional past-to-present reclassifications to drop below the 80% bar, and the only candidate is q01833 (currently gnomic; as event/present the book is still 84% past).
